title: Numbers
summary: Work with trip numbers. Parse and round them, make time slots and length bands, calculate running totals and changes, rank stations, and describe a distribution.

steps.title: Setup: library(tidyverse)
steps.explain: `library(tidyverse)` attaches readr, dplyr and lubridate, whose number functions this lesson uses.

steps.title: Numbers from text, and counts

runs.purpose: pull the numbers out of three bits of text
runs.task: Pull the numbers out of `c("2.35 km", "1,234 trips", "38%")` with `parse_number()`.

runs.purpose: count the trips from each station, busiest first
runs.task: Count the trips from each `start_station`, the busiest first.

steps.explain: `parse_number()` drops whatever surrounds the first number in a string, commas used as thousands separators included, so `"1,234 trips"` becomes 1234. Counting is the most common thing done with numbers in data: `count()` gives each station's trips, and station {top_station} is the busiest, with {top_n}.

steps.title: Slots of 15 minutes: %/% and %%

runs.code:
trips |>
  mutate(minute_of_day = hour(started_at) * 60 + minute(started_at)) |>
  count(slot = minute_of_day %/% 15 * 15, sort = TRUE)

values.top_slot: local({s <- count(mutate(trips, m = hour(started_at) * 60 + minute(started_at)), slot = m %/% 15 * 15, sort = TRUE)$slot[1]; format(s)})
values.top_slot_n: local({s <- count(mutate(trips, m = hour(started_at) * 60 + minute(started_at)), slot = m %/% 15 * 15, sort = TRUE)$n[1]; format(s, big.mark = ",")})
values.top_slot_time: local({s <- count(mutate(trips, m = hour(started_at) * 60 + minute(started_at)), slot = m %/% 15 * 15, sort = TRUE)$slot[1]; sprintf("%d:%02d", s %/% 60, s %% 60)})

runs.purpose: count the trips that started in each 15-minute slot of the day, busiest first
runs.task: Add `minute_of_day`, the minutes since midnight (`hour(started_at) * 60 + minute(started_at)`), then count the trips by `slot = minute_of_day %/% 15 * 15`, the busiest first.

runs.purpose: turn minute 1020 of the day back into hours and minutes
runs.task: Turn 1020 minutes into whole hours with `%/%` and the minutes left over with `%%`, in one vector with `c()`.

steps.explain:
`%/%` divides and drops the remainder, and `%%` gives the remainder. So `minute_of_day %/% 15` numbers each 15-minute slot, and multiplying by 15 turns that back into the minute the slot starts. `* 15` multiplies every value by one number, which R recycles.

The busiest slot starts at minute {top_slot}, with {top_slot_n} trips: `1020 %/% 60` is 17 hours and `1020 %% 60` is 0 minutes left over, so {top_slot_time}.

steps.title: Rounding and cutting into bands

runs.purpose: round three numbers that end in .5

runs.code: trips |> count(band = cut(duration_min, breaks = c(0, 10, 20, 30, 60, Inf)))
alternatives: trips |> mutate(band = cut(duration_min, c(0, 10, 20, 30, 60, Inf))) |> count(band)
runs.purpose: put trip lengths in bands and count trips in each band
runs.task: Count trips by `band`. Make bands by cutting `duration_min` with `cut()` at 0, 10, 20, 30, 60 and `Inf`.

steps.explain:
`round()` rounds a number ending in .5 to the even neighbour, so 0.5 and 2.5 round down and 1.5 up: over many values, the rounding errors cancel out. `floor()` always rounds down, `ceiling()` up, and `round(x, digits = -2)` to the nearest hundred.

`cut()` turns numbers into bands: `(0,10]` means above 0 and up to 10, and holds {n_short} trips. The {n_cut_na} trips of 0 minutes or less fall outside every band, so their band is `NA`.

steps.title: Running totals: cumsum()

runs.purpose: count the trips on each day of the year, as `daily`
runs.task: Count the trips on each `date` (`as_date(started_at)`) and store the result in `daily`.

runs.purpose: add a running total of trips so far
runs.task: Add `running_total`, the total number of trips so far, with `cumsum(n)`.

steps.explain: `cumsum()` adds up as it goes: each day's `running_total` is the trips on that day and every day before it. `cummax()`, `cummin()` and `cummean()` work the same way. The running total passes half the year's trips on {half_date}, well past the middle of the year, because the winter months are quiet.

steps.title: The day before: lag()

runs.code:
daily |>
  mutate(change = n - lag(n)) |>
  slice_max(change, n = 3)
alternatives: daily |> mutate(change = n - lag(n)) |> arrange(desc(change)) |> head(3)

values.jump_date: str_squish(format(slice_max(mutate(daily, change = n - lag(n)), change, n = 1)$date[1], "%A %e %B"))
values.jump: format(slice_max(mutate(daily, change = n - lag(n)), change, n = 1)$change[1])

runs.purpose: work out each day's change from the day before, and show the three biggest rises
runs.task: Add `change`, each day's `n` minus the day before's (`lag(n)`), then keep the three biggest changes with `slice_max()`.

steps.explain: `lag()` shifts a column down one row, so each day sits beside the day before; `lead()` shifts it up. The first day has no day before, so its `change` is `NA`, and `slice_max()` leaves it out. The biggest rise was on {jump_date}: {jump} more trips than the day before, after a rainy or cold day.

steps.title: Ranks within groups: min_rank()

runs.code:
trips |>
  count(start_station, bike_type) |>
  mutate(rank = min_rank(desc(n)), .by = bike_type) |>
  filter(rank <= 3)
alternatives: trips |> count(start_station, bike_type) |> group_by(bike_type) |> mutate(rank = min_rank(desc(n))) |> ungroup() |> filter(rank <= 3)
runs.purpose: rank the stations by trips for each bike type, and keep the top three of each
runs.task: Count trips by `start_station` and `bike_type`. Within each bike type, rank stations with `min_rank(desc(n))` using `.by` in `mutate()`. Keep ranks 1 to 3.

steps.explain:
`min_rank()` numbers values from smallest to largest; `desc()` turns that round, so the busiest station is 1. Tied values share a rank, and the next rank is skipped, as in a race. With `.by`, `mutate()` ranks within each bike type separately, so each has its own top three.

`dense_rank()` doesn't skip ranks after a tie, and `row_number()` breaks ties by position.

steps.title: Centre and spread: summaries

runs.purpose: summarise every trip's length: its minimum, quartiles, mean and maximum

runs.code:
trips |>
  filter(duration_min > 0, duration_min <= 24 * 60) |>
  summarize(
    mean = mean(duration_min),
    median = median(duration_min),
    sd = sd(duration_min),
    q90 = quantile(duration_min, 0.9),
    .by = member_type
  )
alternatives: trips |> filter(duration_min > 0, duration_min <= 1440) |> group_by(member_type) |> summarize(mean = mean(duration_min), median = median(duration_min), sd = sd(duration_min), q90 = quantile(duration_min, 0.9))
runs.purpose: summarise plausible trip lengths for each rider type: mean, median, standard deviation and 90th percentile
runs.task: Keep trips longer than 0 and at most one day. For each `member_type`, find mean, median, standard deviation (`sd()`) and 90th percentile (`quantile(duration_min, 0.9)`) of `duration_min`.

steps.explain:
`summary()` gives a number's minimum, quartiles, median, mean and maximum in one go. The mean, {mean_all} minutes, is well above the median, {median_all}: a few lost bikes' trips of days pull the mean up, while the median, the middle value, doesn't move. Without the implausible trips, the summaries describe real rides.

The mean and median measure the centre; the standard deviation, `sd`, the spread around the mean; and `quantile()` a position: 90% of members' trips last {q90_member} minutes or less, and 90% of casual riders' {q90_casual}.
